design_question: Can smart single-click input and optional automatic skills reduce repetitive inputs while preserving meaningful positioning and risk choices?

context.player_context: Project user on desktop keyboard and mouse; human comparison has not run.
evidence: User explicitly reported that action selection plus two target clicks is cumbersome.
Code review found pending confirmation state and misleading post-action pressure wording.
User confirmed smart left click, right-click autocast, full turn costs, and only an animated border indicator.
context.decision: Adopt requested controls and evaluate whether targeting heuristics need revision.

desired_experience.statement: Less repeated input while keeping intentional positioning, skill and overdrive decisions.
observable_signals: Player can explain the expected hit, push and next telegraphed threat.
Player can disable an unwanted automatic skill directly on its button.

lens.name: decision structure
lens.why: The change affects information, input cost and delegation of choices.
lens.limitations: Fewer clicks cannot prove enjoyment; automated victories cannot replace player judgment.

causal_chain.mechanic: Hover previews and single click commits; right click authorizes repeated legal skill use.
causal_chain.interaction: Player directly selects targets or delegates repeated choices to a reversible heuristic.
causal_chain.dynamic: Fewer confirmation inputs, with some targeting decisions delegated.
causal_chain.perceived_signal: Preview explains consequences and animated border communicates active authorization.
causal_chain.experience: Expected fluency and control, not yet observed in human play.
causal_chain.assumption: Autocast does not steal choices the player values.
causal_chain.evidence: Input tests establish step counts; experiential arrows still require human comparison.

hypotheses.claim: Single click reduces repetition, and optional autocast reduces work for already-decided actions.
hypotheses.change: Replace click-to-preview with hover-to-preview and provide per-skill autocast.
hypotheses.expected_signal: Players need fewer confirmations and can explain when they keep manual control.
hypotheses.falsifier: Accidental commitments or unwanted auto targets dominate, or combat becomes passive waiting.
hypotheses.competing_explanation: Empty encounter space may be the cause of repetitive actions, merely masked by input changes.
hypotheses.unchanged: Damage, cooldowns, enemy response order, map layout, rewards and skill content.

prototype.control: Baseline 1e1ea48 two-click confirmation in matched encounter states.
prototype.variant: First smart click without auto, then matched states with optional automatic skills.
prototype.scope: Target commitment, telegraph understanding, auto cancellation and local choices.
prototype.risks: Learning and encounter-order effects; already-confirmed user preferences are not treated as unapproved.

evidence_plan.participants_context: Invite the project user to play; record prior familiarity and input method. No additional players recruited.
observations: Input chain and accidental actions for basic attacks and skills.
Unwanted auto targets and reasons for disabling a skill.
behavioral_measures: Compare input counts and invalid actions at matched states.
Record immediate auto cancellation or reports of lost intent.
qualitative_prompts: What did you expect to hit and what would respond?
Which automatic cast conflicted with your intention and why?
evidence_plan.decision_rule: Keep direct inputs if they reduce repetition without confusing outcomes; revise auto targeting if it repeatedly conflicts with intent. If repetitive encounters dominate, prioritize encounter design instead of increasing damage.
integrity_checks: Match rules, enemies and positions and record whether auto is enabled.
Record comparison order, familiarity and input device.
Separate engineering tests from human play and disclose manipulated fixtures.

ethics.dark_patterns: No hidden cost, spending pressure or new real-time battle punishment; auto is directly reversible.
ethics.accessibility: Use shape and text for targets; border animation follows user preference with tooltip text. Reduced animation options remain unimplemented.
ethics.privacy: Only necessary local test evidence; human feedback is voluntary.

decisions.decision: Adopt user-approved smart click and per-skill automatic casting with existing turn resolution.
decisions.basis: Explicit user choice and reproducible input burden; enjoyment remains untested.

route_out.next_owner: Interaction refinement and human playtest review
route_out.reason: After technical checks, assess whether automatic targeting fits intent and encounters remain meaningful.
